rulings.challenge_claim: LF (lf_cluster_c06_r1, item P05-011): the row's rejected_alternative states Prov.10.7 'does not continue into 10:6's head/mouth imagery' -- true for that image, but omits a rarer shared root connecting the two verses (sweep.py --skel blessing-root, 8 verses book-wide, with 10:6 and 10:7 adjacent hits), undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-ran sweep.py --skel ברכ (skeleton tier, object named: the ברכ consonantal spelling). Reproduced LF's exact 8-verse, 8-ref hit list byte-for-byte: Prov.10.6, Prov.10.7, Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26, Prov.24.25, Prov.28.20 (verse-count unit, skeleton tier). Confirmed from verse_map_oshb.json (byte tier) that Prov.10.6 opens בְּ֭רָכוֹת ('blessings') and Prov.10.7 carries לִבְרָכָ֑ה ('for a blessing') at its B-line -- adjacent verses, same consonantal root, contiguous skeleton match. Checked the row's actual text (draft_rows_combined.jsonl, writer_decision_id P05-011): its rejected_alternative reads 'Grouping with either neighbor was rejected: 10:6 turns on head and mouth, 10:8 on heart and lips, and neither body-part pair recurs in this verse's memory/name contrast' -- this addresses ONLY the body-part-imagery axis and is silent on the blessing root, matching TOOLKIT.md's CROSS-SEAM COHESION standing rule: a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. ALLOGRAPHY CHECK (per assignment instruction, name the object): the 8-verse hit-list is the MEDIAL-form ברכ spelling specifically -- both cited verses use this spelling. A parallel sweep of the FINAL-form spelling ברך (per TOOLKIT.md's own final-letter-allography rule: 'preserved exactly, sweep per attested spelling') returns a DISJOINT 5-verse set -- Prov.3.33, Prov.20.21, Prov.22.9, Prov.27.14, Prov.30.11 -- zero overlap with the medial set. LF's prose calls this 'a rare shared root' and its tier_citations label the object 'blessing-root (skeleton sweep, object=ברכ lexeme)'; per TOOLKIT.md's SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE (name the swept object as spelling vs term vs root, THEN count; blended sweeps forbidden), the precise object is the ברכ SPELLING, not the full root (root-level would need both spellings named and totalled at 13, not 8). Because both 10:6 and 10:7 actually use the medial spelling, LF's digit (8) and ref-list are byte-accurate for the object as cited and need no numeric correction -- only the citation label should read 'spelling' rather than 'root' going forward. OL's own P05-011 item is a SUPPORT, not a competing challenge: it verifies the body-part non-overlaps (10:6 head/mouth, 10:8 heart/lips) from the bytes and is correct on that narrower claim, but never ran a blessing-spelling sweep, so it neither confirms nor contradicts LF's finding -- an evidentiary gap in OL's coverage, not a primary-vs-primary conflict to reconcile.
rulings.remedy: SEAM-PAIR CURE, authored once for P05-010 and P05-011 together (Job lesson a) -- both rows' rejected_alternative fields get one consistent edit citing the SAME digit and object label. P05-010's own LF packet item (lf_cluster_c06.json, same attempt lf_cluster_c06_r1) raises the identical gap on the 10:6 side with the same 8-verse ברכ evidence; that item is already r1-adjudicated, so this follow-on does not re-rule it, but the two remedies must read as one work order: (1) P05-010's rejected_alternative adds, after its existing head/mouth-vs-memory/name sentence, a clause naming בְּ֭רָכוֹת (10:6) and its match to 10:7's לִבְרָכָ֑ה, citing 'the ברכ spelling, 8 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel)', and explains it is stock blessing/curse-frame vocabulary recurring in a different grammatical form (bare plural noun at 10:6 vs. prefixed noun at 10:7), not a distinguishing catchword -- parallel to how the row's own device_notes already treats the 10:6/10:11 B-line repeat as 'a recurring formula texture across the chapter, not a local-adjacency device'. (2) P05-011's rejected_alternative gets the mirror clause: after its existing 10:6/10:8 body-part sentence, add that 10:6's בְּ֭רָכוֹת does share this verse's root ('the ברכ spelling, 8 verses book-wide') but as the same stock blessing-frame vocabulary in a different grammatical form, not a distinguishing catchword. Neither remedy changes unit_type, span, or confidence -- both rows stay single_proverb per the C2 atomic default; this is a disclosure-and-refutation fix only. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original, Job lesson b): re-running sweep.py --skel ברכ against the revised rejected_alternative text of BOTH rows must show the 8-verse digit and the ברכ object explicitly named and refuted in each row's own prose (not merely present in boundary_evidence_refs); check_universals.py must not flag either row for an undisclosed adjacent-verse device; citation_sweep.py must pass on both rows post-edit.
